newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank stocks rally as bonds continue higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank stocks rally as bonds continue higher.

text.p: U.S. bank stocks rallied Tuesday in response to a continued upward move in long term interest rates which in turn reflected weak economic data.
Housing starts fell 5.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.366 million units, the lowest monthly reading in a year.
The long Treasury bond was up 17/32 at midday, dropping the yield to 6.43 percent.
"The (banking) group is strong right across the board," said analyst Frank Barkocy of Josephthal, Lyon & Ross Inc. "It's a reaction to this morning's economic data."

Chase Manhattan Corp was up 1-1/8 to 90-5/8 at midday after making a new 12-month high at 91-1/2. NationsBank Corp was up 1-3/8 to a new high of 98-1/2. Summit Bancorp was up 3/4 to 44-1/8 after making a new high at 44-1/4.
Trude Latimer, an independent analyst based in Charlottesville, Va., said some investors appeared to be buying Chase Manhattan and other big banks as part of a general interest in big name stocks.
Barkocy said the larger capitalization bank stocks were providing the leadership for the group.

Asked if bank stocks would be vulnerable if the U.S. stock market went into a downward correction, Barkocy said he would not expect them to be as vulnerable as some of the high technology stocks. He said the industry generally has solid underlying fundamentals.

The analyst said in the current euphoric enviroment he was telling clients to consider taking profits in stocks with big gains, such as KeyCorp, and consider new positons in stocks like Fleet Financial Group Inc, BankBoston Corp, Huntington Bancshares Inc and HUBCO Inc.
KeyCorp was up 3/8 at 49-5/8, a new 12-month high.
